mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-to-week rebound in WORKPLACES after t-1w should spill into higher retail footfall within four weeks because more commuting days create more lunch and after-work purchases. This mechanism predicts RETAIL_REC rises when WORKPLACES stops falling and turns upward.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -27.7 to -10.4 while TRANSIT stayed around -25
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays near or above its t-0w level for the next month but RETAIL_REC does not move above its last-4-week mean, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT below the current low should push RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks because fewer station trips reduce incidental shopping and city-centre visits. The effect is strongest if the transit drop is not offset by a compensating rise in workplaces mobility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 after remaining above -30
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -24.6 at t-0w after -24.6 at t-3w and -27.1 at t-2w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -30 and RETAIL_REC is still unchanged or higher two weeks later, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM continues to cool, households are substituting toward home-based routines and fewer discretionary outings. That pattern should suppress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above 12 and GROCERY_PHARM fell from 11.9 to 1.7
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week average within 28 days, this interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The steep drop in PARKS suggests colder or wetter conditions that reduce general outing intensity and indirectly lower shopping trips. If PARKS stays deeply negative over the next month, RETAIL_REC should also remain below its recent average.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20 and remains there for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 5.6 at t-3w to -30.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -20 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC turns above its previous four-week mean, the seasonal suppression mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM usually indicates more essential errands and neighborhood trip-making, which then supports nearby retail visits within one week. This should lift RETAIL_REC only when grocery activity is rising from a depressed base.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points week-on-week after being below 5
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from 11.9 to 1.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points from a low base and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain suppressed, the city is still operating under a constrained-mobility regime that limits discretionary shopping trips. In that regime, RETAIL_REC should keep drifting lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both still negative at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -20 and RETAIL_REC rises over the next month, the constrained-mobility mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in WORKPLACES after the recent trough should first boost TRANSIT and then feed retail spending through commuting corridors within two weeks. The effect is strongest if the WORKPLACES rebound is sustained rather than a one-week bounce.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved sharply from -27.7 to -10.4 while TRANSIT stayed subdued
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks but TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC do not improve within two weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a winter pullback in parks use, discretionary outing intensity should remain weak and retail-and-recreation mobility should stay below the prior four-week average. The signal matters only when PARKS is falling while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -24.9 to -30.1 and RESIDENTIAL stayed above 12
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps falling and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises in the following week, the seasonal-homebound mechanism fails.
